output.text: MANILA, Philippines — Iniimbestigahan ng National Bureau of Investigation-Homicide Division ang pagkamatay ng isang ginang na sumailalim sa liposuction, tummy tuck, Brazilian butt lift, at bodytite for arms ng isang celebrity plastic surgeon, sa San Juan City noong Marso, 2, 2026. Ang American-based Filipino-American reality television na si Ronn Tristan Perez, anak ng nasawi, ang personal na nagtungo sa NBI noong Huwebes. Batay sa mga ulat, ang biktimang si Gng. Casteel ay nagbayad ng P570,000 para sa nasabing procedures na umabot ng pitong oras, na-discharge matapos ang 3 araw na recovery period. Subalit pagkalipas ng apat na araw ay isinugod siya sa ospital at na-diagnosed ng “high-risk pulmonary embolisim” o isang medical emergency dahil sa blood clot na humarang sa daloy ng dugo sa baga at mapanganib na hindi normal na presyon ng dugo. Nag-aalala aniya, siya sa nakitang hitsura ng ina nang makausap sa Face Time habang nasa klinika. “I FaceTime her, and she’s pale, she’s missing a tooth. I said, ‘What’s happening, Mom?’ Me and my brother were both worried,” ani Perez. Ilang araw ang lumipas nang makatanggap siya ng tawag mula sa tiyo at ama na binawian ng buhay ang ina. Hindi aniya, niya nakuha ang gusto niyang makita nang ibigay ang medical records ng ina. “I’m not accusing anyone of anything. I need more than that. I need documents, papers, expertise that what was done here is everything that was supposed to be done. No stones left unturned,” aniya sa isang interview. Payo niya sa sinumang nais magpa-enhance o magpaganda na kahit mabilis na pag-Google lang ay dapat munang alamin ang mga delikadong bagay at magdoble ingat habang ginagawa at pagkatapos ng procedures. output.title: Evidence in actor's death points to suicide
output.description: Though investigators have yet to release their findings on the death of 27-year-old actor Tyron Perez, the initial results of two tests indicate he may have committed suicide, a police official said yesterday.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines - Though investigators have yet to release their findings on the death of 27-year-old actor Tyron Perez, the initial results of two tests indicate he may have committed suicide, a police official said yesterday. Senior Police Officer 3 Armando Delima said that the Northern Police District crime lab already have the results of the paraffin test on Perez and the ballistic examination on the .22 caliber revolver recovered beside his body but it would still be confirmed by the Camp Crame crime lab. “All indications, from testimonies of the witnesses including Perez’s kin, and the circumstances within the victim’s car, point to a suicide, yet these are not conclusive unless the official findings of the crime lab would come out,” Delima said. Delima declined to divulge the results of the NPD crime lab findings, claiming that it would only be released once verified by the Camp Crame crime lab. Perez, a GMA-7 Starstruck reality show talent before he joined ABS-CBN’s Star Magic, was found by his friends Jonathan Koo and Priscilla Salazar on the back seat of his black Toyota Altis (ZSP-675) parked near his friends’ house, where he had been staying after he and his wife quarreled. “The victim’s car was locked inside and we needed to break its glass window to open it. Nothing shows there was a struggle and nothing was also taken from his things,” Delima said. According to Salazar, a few days before Perez was found dead, he confided to her about his problem with his wife, Liv Espino Perez, and of his debt in a casino. output.title: IN PHOTOS: 8 celebrities who admitted to having plastic surgery | ABS-CBN Entertainment
output.description: While there's a sense that plastic surgery is no longer taboo in the country, there's still very few celebrities who are comfortable in openly owning up to goin
output.text: While there's a sense that plastic surgery is no longer taboo in the country, there are still very few celebrities who are comfortable in openly owning up to going under the knife. That's why it feels refreshing to have someone like Xander Ford not only admit it, but unveil his new look in such a grand manner. With that in mind, here are the other celebrities who have no qualms in sharing that they had something done to improve their overall appearance. Vice Ganda No stranger to being real, the "It's Showtime" host said he had his hips enhanced so he can wear more revealing outfits in his shows. "Wala naman yatang maniniwala kapag sinabi kong totoo ang balakang ko, talaga namang gawa," he said. Jake Zyrus After coming out as a transgender man, Jake Zyrus, formerly Charice, revealed that he underwent breast removal surgery, a decision which, he said in an inteview , made him feel that his transition was "complete." Rufa Mae Quinto In an interview back in 2014, the sexy comedienne openly talked about her breast implants and having it removed because her left breast had been hurting for a year. Angeline Quinto Four years ago, the singer shared that undergoing various cosmetic procedures served as a much-needed confidence booster for her. She said she had double eyelid surgery and liposuction on her arms and back. Lani Misalucha The "Asia's Nightingale" readily admitted to having her teeth, nose, and chin done, saying that she wants to look more confident in front of the camera. "Who doesn't want to look good?" she asked. Christopher de Leon The 60-year-old actor looks great as ever, but he did admit to getting a little help from cosmetic enhancements to maintain his youthful look. In 2011, he said that several procedures have managed to keep his face thin and firm, as well as his lower eyelids look less puffy. Gretchen Barretto She confirmed to Pep back in 2009 that she had her lips done, explaining that she wanted to have more pouty lips. "They say it's sexy, 'di ba when you have pouty lips? That's why I pout a lot," she said. Kitkat The comedienne stated in 2006 that she had her nose and boobs done. "Kung makaka-improve ba ito ng personality ko at makakadagdag ng confidence ko, bakit ako tatanggi, 'di ba?"

output.title: Proud Retokada: 7 Celebrities Who Underwent Cosmetic Procedures | Push Pins | ABS-CBN Entertainment
output.description: These celebrities are out and proud about the cosmetic procedures they underwent in order to enhance their appearance.
output.text: 1. Angeline Quinto Angeline Quinto has never been ashamed about going under the knife. The Kapamilya singer has admitted to having several cosmetic procedures done. Among these were eyelid surgery, arm liposuction, belly liposuction, Thermage, breast reduction, and Glutathione injections. 2. Janine Berdin Recently, Janine Berdin became the talk of the town after photos of her showcasing her major transformation went viral. Speculations from netizens then arose, claiming that the singer underwent plastic surgery. In an interview with Vice Ganda, Janine addressed the issue and admitted to undergoing a procedure to enhance the appearance of her nose. Janine also revealed that it was her insecurity that urged her to go through the procedure and that she is happy with her new look. 3. Chienna Filomeno In 2019, after numerous speculations on whether she went under the knife or not, GirlTrends member Chienna Filomeno finally broke her silence. In a 2019 interview in Tonight With Boy Abunda , Chienna admitted to getting a nose job. She also revealed that the procedure was a corrective measure for an injury she had obtained as a newborn baby and not merely for vanity. 4. Vice Ganda Unkabogable Star Vice Ganda is also an open book when it comes to his body and appearance. The comedian-actor admitted to getting botox. He also underwent a hip enhancement surgery. 5. Beauty Gonzalez Gone are the days of the chubby, outspoken 17-year-old from Dumaguete who graced the reality show Pinoy Big Brother back in 2008. Beauty Gonzalez has since undergone cosmetic procedures to enhance her appearance. The Kapamilya actress admitted to getting liposuction to remove unwanted fats from her arms, jawline, and chin. 6. Morissette Amon In a 2018 Rated K interview, Asia’s Phoenix Morissette Amon revealed that she’s always been insecure about her arms. Despite going to the gym, she didn’t notice a significant improvement in the size of her arms. This is what urged Morissette to go under the knife and get an arm liposuction procedure. She admitted that going through it was a big boost to her confidence. 7. Nathalie Hart In an interview with Boy Abunda in 2018, actress Nathalie Hart admitted that she’s had multiple enhancements. Aside from her lip tattoos and eyebrow tattoos, the actress revealed she also underwent breast augmentation. Nathalie said it is her way of handling her insecurity. Learn more about their cosmetic procedures here: What can you say about their enhancements?

output.title: NBI probes Taguig flood projects; DOJ says no order issued
output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is investigating flood control projects in Taguig City, even as the Department of Justice (DOJ) clarified Monday that it did not order the probe.
output.text: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Monday said it started its investigation into flood control projects in Taguig City, even as the Department of Justice (DOJ) clarified Monday that it did not order the probe. NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the bureau was already looking into 11 flood control projects implemented in 2022 that were allegedly linked to some of the country's top 15 contractors. “In fact, we are already investigating, kasi nung 2022 merong 11 proyekto diyan na somehow related doon sa mga pinangalanan na Top 15 contractors,” Matibag told reporters. (In fact, we are already investigating because, in 2022, there were 11 projects there that were somehow linked to those named among the top 15 contractors.) “Baka sabihin ninyo timing na naman. Anyway, public na naman ‘yan dahil sinasabi ni Senator Lacson, so I think we should mention it,” he added. (You might say this is about timing again. Anyway, this is already public knowledge because Senator Lacson mentioned it, so I think we should mention it.) Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, however, stressed that the DOJ did not direct the NBI to conduct the investigation, saying the bureau was acting under its own mandate. “We will respect the independence of the NBI relative to their mandate to pursue investigations. First thing, hindi ito pinag-utos ng DOJ. This is pursuant to the mandate of the NBI to pursue all this,” Vida said. (We will respect the independence of the NBI in carrying out its mandate to pursue investigations. First, the DOJ did not order this. This is pursuant to the NBI's mandate to pursue these matters.) Vida said that should the case reach the DOJ, the department would act based on the evidence presented. “Kung sakaling makarating sa DOJ ‘yan, it will be based on what are the pieces of evidence presented. Rule of law pa rin tayo,” he said. (If that reaches the DOJ, our action will be based on the evidence presented. We still abide by the rule of law.) On Sunday, Senate Blue Ribbon Committee chairperson Senator Erwin Tulfo told fellow Senator Alan Peter Cayetano to be ready for an investigation into Taguig's flood control projects. Cayetano's brother, former Taguig Mayor and current PTV general manager Lino Cayetano, who served as city mayor from 2019 to 2022, had sought an investigation into P6 billion worth of flood control projects implemented in Taguig from 2022 to 2025. Vida also said ongoing investigations by other agencies should not be viewed as a distraction for senator-judges. “Hindi dapat dahil ‘yung paghahabol natin ng accountability, hindi naman tumitigil ‘yun. Pare-parehong may ginagampanan, at ginagalang natin ang mga Senator-Judges,” Vida said. (It should not be, because our pursuit of accountability does not stop. We all have our respective roles to play, and we respect the senator-judges.) “And sa akin, kung wala namang dapat ipangamba about sa rule of law, wala dapat ipangamba ang mga senator-judges,” he added. (And for me, if there is nothing to fear from the rule of law, then the senator-judges have nothing to fear.) According to Vida, the NBI investigation is not yet barred by prescription, meaning authorities may still legally investigate and prosecute any alleged offenses arising from the projects. — MCG GMA News

output.title: NBI investigates 18 ex-Marines’ credibility, cash delivery allegations
output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is investigating the credibility and claim of 18 alleged former Marines that they delivered cash to public officials and personalities, Director Melvin Matibag said Wednesday.
output.text: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is investigating the credibility and claim of 18 alleged former Marines that they delivered cash to public officials and personalities, Director Melvin Matibag said Wednesday. In an ambush interview, Matibag said the Office of the Ombudsman deputized the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) to conduct the investigation. “Ang ginawa muna namin, chineck muna namin ‘yung personalities because there was a report that some of them were not really members of the Marine Corp, which turns out to be upon verification, totoo pala,” he said. (What we did first was check the personalities because there was a report that some of them were not really members of the Marine Corps, which turned out upon verification to be true.) “Some of them, in fact, have some cases, criminal cases. So may mga ganon na kaming nakikita. And we’re looking on the incident itself,” he added. (Some of them, in fact, have some cases, criminal cases. So we are already seeing things like that. And we’re looking at the incident itself.) Aside from this, Matibag said they are looking into the people behind this, as well as the individual that notarized their affidavit. To recall, lawyer Levito Baligod and the 18 ex-Marines accused several individuals of allegedly receiving cash from former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co. The government officials and individuals mentioned have denied the allegations against them, with the Philippine Navy saying that four of the 18 were never members of the Navy nor the Philippine Marine Corps. Matibag said that the Ombudsman has the power to deputize any agency in line with their mandate. “NBI has already been deputized by the Office of the Ombudsman to investigate on the incident, ‘yung sa 18 marines, ‘yung kanilang joint affidavit and all the allegations,” he said. “We investigate all the angles. Lahat titignan namin,” he added. He said that based on the process of investigation, they must first look into the complaint and the complainants “We look at the personality, we look at the veracity of the statement and if the evidence will lead towards their allegations, doon sa mga binanggit na pangalan, we will call upon them,” he said. He also stressed that there is nothing political about the investigation. “We look in every angle. This is not political. But we look at the angle, personalities involved, personalities that were mentioned,” he said. —AOL GMA Integrated News

output.title: NBI to file raps over P55 million SEAG cauldron
output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation is set to file cases in the coming days over alleged irregularities related to the “golden cauldron” installed for the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation is set to file cases in the coming days over alleged irregularities related to the “golden cauldron” installed for the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said. Speaking at a forum in Quezon City over the weekend, Matibag said the investigation had yielded documents and testimonies that could support criminal charges. “Within the next few days, perhaps within a week, we will be filing cases,” Matibag said. The investigation is part of the NBI’s broader probe into the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC), which Matibag said involves multiple cases and a large volume of documents and testimonies. “We divided this into pieces so we can file cases. There will be different cases coming out. The cauldron is another case. That might be the first one,” he said. Matibag said the NBI had obtained documents concerning the cauldron, which reportedly cost P55 million, although the actual cost was allegedly only about P5 million. He said several leaders of sports associations were also being investigated, with some already appearing before the NBI after receiving subpoenas. Matibag said the NBI was also examining the activities of people associated with Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano, who was the head of PHISGOC in 2019. He identified sports executive Ramon Suzara as among those being looked into, noting that some PHISGOC members had been Cayetano’s colleagues, staff members or associates. “We are still developing and checking what ventures they are involved in,” Matibag said. The NBI is also looking into why PHISGOC continued to sponsor international events despite being created specifically to organize the 2019 SEA Games. “It was supposed to end its existence after the SEA Games. But we found out that until now, they are still sponsoring international events. We are looking into that,” Matibag said. Matibag stressed that the PHISGOC investigation remains ongoing and that the NBI is pursuing separate cases based on the evidence it has gathered. output.title: NBI to summon DPWH officials, contractors
output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation will subpoena contractors and officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways in connection with questionable flood control projects in the district of Davao City Rep. Paolo Duterte.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) will subpoena contractors and officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) in connection with questionable flood control projects in the district of Davao City Rep. Paolo Duterte. NBI Director Melvin Matibag yesterday said the bureau obtained documents from the DPWH showing 47 of 100 flood control projects implemented in Duterte’s district have been flagged for further investigation. These projects include those suspected to be ghost or not delivered as well as those that appeared to be substandard and located in similar areas, but have different titles and separate funding. “Out of the 47 flood control projects, about six are clearly questionable based on documents we have reviewed. We will be issuing subpoenas either tomorrow or Monday,” Matibag told journalists. The NBI said it has identified at least three construction firms linked to the projects and plans to summon company representatives as part of the investigation. The bureau initially identified a P1.9-billion allocation for Duterte’s district, which was awarded to Genesis 88, whose owner is allegedly close to the lawmaker. Matibag clarified that Duterte is not among those being summoned for now, saying the agency would first focus on the contractors, and DPWH officials and personnel linked to the projects. The investigation is being handled by the NBI Task Force “Flood Control,” which was created to look into anomalous government projects. output.title: PROFILE: Who is Melvin Matibag, the prosecution’s final witness on alleged threats? | ABS-CBN News
output.description: The testimony of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag was at the center of Vice President Sara Duterte’s eighth day of impeachment tri
output.text: NBI Director Melvin Matibag takes the witness stand on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — The testimony of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag was at the center of Vice President Sara Duterte’s eighth day of impeachment trial and continues on Wednesday. Matibag is the prosecution’s final witness for the fourth article, which accuses Duterte of committing grave threats against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and his relatives and inciting to sedition through said alleged threats. Impeachment Trial of Sara Duterte His appearance came months after he was appointed as NBI chief. Before joining the Marcos administration, however, Matibag was considered an ally of the vice president’s father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, having held several key posts during the previous administration. A TEACHERS’ SON Matibag’s parents began their careers as teachers before later joining government service. His father taught at Claro M. Recto High School, while his mother served as a teacher at Pedro Pelaez Elementary School. He is married to Laguna First District Rep. Ma. Rene Ann Matibag. A lawyer by profession, Matibag earned his undergraduate degree in Philosophy from the University of Santo Tomas before obtaining his law degree from the Ateneo de Manila University in 1996. He was admitted to the Philippine bar the following year and later completed a master’s degree in corporate and finance law at Wayne State University in Detroit, Michigan. TIES TO THE DUTERTES Former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo appointed Matibag as general manager of the Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) in 2010. In 2014, he served as convenor of Movement for Reform, Continuity and Momentum (More2Come), a group that advocated to amend the 1987 Constitution to allow then-President Benigno “Noynoy” Aquino III to seek another term. In 2017, the older Duterte appointed Matibag as president of the National Transmission Corporation (TransCo). Matibag later became acting secretary-general of Duterte’s political party, Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban), during a leadership dispute that split the party into two. In 2022, Duterte appointed him as acting cabinet secretary, a position that was later abolished by the Marcos administration. Matibag resigned as PDP-Laban acting secretary-general in 2023, saying his personal principles were no longer aligned with the party's direction. He also said he wanted to avoid any appearance of a conflict of interest because his wife belonged to a different political party. TIMELINE: The cracks in ruling party PDP-Laban before BBM endorsement OPINION PIECES AGAINST DUTERTE After leaving PDP-Laban, Matibag returned to private law practice and entered the academe, becoming the first dean of the Lyceum of Alabang College of Law. He also became a columnist for the Daily Tribune, where he wrote about the vice president. In October 2023, Matibag wrote in his column that he opposed the allocation of confidential and intelligence funds to the Office of the Vice President. He argued that the Constitution does not assign the vice president functions that would require such funds. At the time, he emphasized that his position was directed at the policy rather than Vice President Duterte personally. But nearly a year later, Matibag criticized Duterte in a September 2024 column and described her as a “bratinella” or a spoiled brat. In November of the same year, following Duterte’s controversial livestream that formed part of the impeachment case against her, Matibag published another opinion column. Matibag criticized Duterte’s remarks in the livestream and described her actions as “an ambitious power grab” that resulted in her “humiliating defeat.” He also again referred to her as a “bratinella.” At the impeachment trial, Matibag explained that it was the older Duterte who first used the moniker for her daughter, the vice president. SHIFT TO THE MARCOS ADMINISTRATION In September 2024, Matibag filed a disbarment complaint against former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque, a staunch ally of the Dutertes and his colleague during the Duterte administration. Matibag said the complaint included issues related to Roque's social media posts, including the so-called “polvoron” video involving Marcos. In August 2025, Matibag sought to return to government service by applying for the vacant position of Ombudsman but was not selected for the post. Instead, Marcos appointed him NBI director on February 19, 2026. This is also in the same period that a second round of impeachment complaints against Duterte were filed at the House of Representatives. Following his appointment, some questioned whether his selection was linked to his complaint against Roque. output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has started its investigation into the reported death threats against Senator Risa Hontiveros, according to NBI Direc
output.text: MANILA — The National Bureau of Investigation has started its investigation into reported death threats against Sen. Risa Hontiveros, bureau director Melvin Matibag said. He said Hontiveros' office had reached out to him and that the NBI is already gathering evidence, including examining the social media posts where the threats were allegedly made. 'I do not think it was fair': Hontiveros, Pia Cayetano clash over ‘improper’ trial question “We are just waiting for the formal documentation, but we are already in the process of investigating this,” Matibag said. The NBI chief said the investigation will follow the same procedure applied to other cases “After the case build-up, if we feel that it is enough for us to file a case, we will file it with the [Department of Justice],” Matibag said. He said the social media posts containing the alleged threats have been endorsed to the NBI’s Cybercrime Division and forensic laboratory for proper examination. He also expressed concern over what he described as the increasing normalization of death threats, particularly against public officials. NBI probe into Duterte 'hitman' narrowed down to 20 names—Matibag “[T]his is very alarming,” Matibag said. He warned that threats against government officials should not be taken lightly, stressing that such acts could have broader implications. “If even our government officials who are high-ranking can be threatened ordinarily, that is where I say our national security will be under attack,” he said. Prosecution 'respects' Cayetano siblings' qualms vs NBI's Matibag Matibag assured the publlic that the NBI will pursue the case based on evidence and in accordance with the law, regardless of political considerations. “We will do our mandate as to law and order. But make no mistake, this will not be political or personal. We will base our actions on evidence and according to the process and to the law,” Matibag said.
